findings.evidence: Lines 84–99 define `characterLp` solely using `ContinuousMap.toLp` and identify its representative via `character_apply`; no inner product, conjugation, orthonormal basis, or `RCLike` operation occurs there. The underlying `character` is already declared under the weaker assumptions at `Continuous/Character.lean:76–104`.
findings.fix: Move these three declarations to a section with `[NontriviallyNormedField 𝕜] [CompleteSpace 𝕜] [NormedAddCommGroup V] [NormedSpace 𝕜 V] [FiniteDimensional 𝕜 V]`, retaining `RCLike` and inner-product assumptions only for `inner_characterLp_eq_sum` and the orthogonality results.
findings.issue: `characterLp`, `characterLp_def`, and `coeFn_characterLp` inherit `[RCLike 𝕜]` and `[InnerProductSpace 𝕜 V]`, although they only package the already-general continuous character in `Lp`; this excludes finite-dimensional normed representations over other complete nontrivially normed fields.

summary: The basic `L²` character packaging remains unnecessarily restricted to real/complex inner-product representations.
